Calculation of Glucose Absorbed
in Peritoneal Dialysis (PD) Patients
The net glucose absorption from dialysate should
be taken into account when calculating total energy
intake for PD patients. There have been many published
formulas estimating the kcal absorbed from peritoneal
dialysate. The most accurate method is to measure the
grams of glucose in the efﬂ uent and compare this with 
the grams of glucose that were infused. Generally, in 
PD patients with normal peritoneal transport capac-
ity, approximately 60% of the daily dialysate glucose 
load is absorbed—this results in a glucose absorption
of approximately 100 to 200 g of glucose per 24 hours.
Another method that considers dialysis modality and
membrane transport characteristics is the following
formula:1
glucose absorbed (kcal)  (1  D/D0)xi
where D/D0 is the fraction of glucose remaining and the
xi is the initial glucose.
Example: infused  4 L of 38 g/L  4L of 13.6 g/L
 152  54.4  206 g  xi
Measured remaining glucose
 1200 mg/dL in 10 L efﬂ uent
 1200  (10,000 mL/100,000)
 1200  0.1
 120 g
D/D0  120/206  0.58
  (1  0.58)  206  86.5 g
  86.5  3.4  294 kcal
